# Additions to Esther Chapter 2 (Addition B) — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther B | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_002_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition B: The full text of King Artaxerxes's decree ordering the destruction of the Jews. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 3:13.]*

**2:1** The following is a copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes writes to the governors of the hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India to Ethiopia, and to those set-under them, as follows:

**2:2** Having become ruler over many nations and having gained dominion over the whole world, I determined — not being lifted-up by the presumption of power but always governing with equity and gentleness —

**2:3** to make the lives of my subjects continuously tranquil, and making my kingdom both ordered and peaceable and accessible to all in its extent — to-wish what the-nations desire, restoring the welcome peace of all men.

**2:4** But when I asked my counselors how this-thing was to-be-accomplished, Haman — who excels in wisdom among us and is distinguished for his steadfast goodwill and unshakeable trustworthiness, and has gained the-second rank in-the kingdom —

**2:5** explained to us that there-is mingled among all the-nations a certain hostile people, opposed in-its laws to every nation, and continually setting-at-nothing the-commands of-the king, so that the-administration of-our kingdom which we-honorably-manage cannot be-brought-to-completion.

**2:6** Having-understood therefore that this nation alone stands continually in-opposition to all mankind, using strange mixtures of laws, and ill-disposed toward our governance, doing as much evil as it-is-able and not practicing the things-that-are-good of-the state,

**2:7** we-command that those indicated to you in the-letters written by Haman, who-is appointed over the-affairs and is a second father to us, all-together with their wives and children shall-be-utterly-destroyed by the-swords of-the enemies, without any pity or mercy, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month — that-is Adar — of-the present year,

**2:8** so that those who-were formerly and are now hostile may in-a-single day go-down by violence into Hades, and may leave our-affairs-hereafter continually stable and untroubled."
